faq.label: Frequently asked questions
faq.title: Frequently asked questions about Bergson mini excavators

items.q: How do I transport a mini excavator to a construction site?
items.a: Our mini excavators fit on a typical car trailer up to 3.5 t GVW. In practice, transport on a trailer with a passenger car or van is not a problem.

items.q: How long does mini excavator delivery take?
items.a: Models available in Poland are usually delivered within 5-14 business days. We confirm the exact date during the quotation because it depends on current availability and delivery location.

items.q: How long does generator delivery take?
items.a: Most generators from the current offer are delivered within 15-20 business days. The date depends on the engine variant and current availability of the specific model.

items.q: Can I buy for a company and use leasing?
items.a: Yes. We issue a VAT invoice, work with leasing companies and help with the paperwork. The instalment for BM13 starts from about PLN 480 net per month with 60-month leasing.

items.q: What happens if something breaks after the warranty?
items.a: After the warranty ends, we still provide paid mobile service and sell parts from our Polish warehouse. This means you are not left alone with the machine after the first year.

items.q: Can I see the machine in person before buying?
items.a: Yes. By prior appointment, we show machines in Antoniewo and Pobórka Wielka. Contact us and we will confirm the nearest date and correct location.

items.q: Are the machines new and CE-certified?
items.a: All machines are brand new, with a CE declaration of conformity. We include full technical documentation and an operator manual in Polish.

gwarancja.title: Warranty terms
gwarancja.intro: This document sets out the rules for granting and performing the warranty for Bergson Machines Goods. This document forms an integral part of the Bergson Machines Sales Terms.

blocks.text: The warranty for Bergson Machines Goods is granted by Better Solutions Spółka z ograniczoną odpowiedzialnością with its registered office in Czapury (61-160), ul. Poznańska 7, KRS: 0000837608, NIP: 7252298652, hereinafter referred to as the Warranty Provider.
The warranty is granted voluntarily and does not exclude, limit or suspend the Buyer’s rights arising from regulations on non-conformity of goods with the contract.

The warranty covers physical defects of the Goods arising from causes inherent in the Goods themselves, provided normal use is maintained in accordance with the operator manual supplied by the Warranty Provider.

items: BM10, BM12, BM12C mini excavators - 12 months from the date the Goods are released to the Buyer;
working attachments (buckets, hammers, augers) - 12 months from the date of release;
spare parts supplied as part of a warranty repair - 3 months or until the end of the original warranty period, whichever expires later.
mechanical, electrical or hydraulic damage caused by the Buyer or third parties;
defects resulting from improper operation, maintenance or attachment installation contrary to the instructions;
natural wear of consumable elements, in particular filters, oils, seals, rubber hoses, rubber and steel tracks, bulbs and fuses;
damage caused by using the Goods contrary to their intended purpose, overloading or lack of regular service inspections;
defects caused by the use of non-original spare parts or operating fluids not approved by the manufacturer;
damage resulting from force majeure, including flood, fire, lightning strike or frost below the permissible operating temperature;
Goods with damaged or illegible serial numbers.

blocks.text: Step 1 - Defect notification. The Buyer is obliged to report the defect immediately after discovering it, no later than within 14 days, by e-mail to: kontakt@bergsonmachines.pl.

items: a precise description of the identified defect together with photo or video documentation;
the machine serial number from the nameplate;
the purchase date and a copy of proof of purchase, in particular a VAT invoice or receipt;
the Buyer’s contact details and the location where the Goods are located.

blocks.text: Step 2 - Claim assessment. The Warranty Provider confirms receipt of the claim within 2 business days and indicates whether the repair will be performed at the place of use of the Goods or whether the Goods must be delivered to a service point.

Step 3 - Execution. The Warranty Provider reviews the warranty claim and begins execution within 14 business days of its proper delivery. If the complaint is accepted, the Warranty Provider will, at its own discretion, repair the Goods, deliver and install a spare part, or replace the Goods with defect-free Goods.
Step 4 - Collection of Goods. After the repair is completed, the Warranty Provider notifies the Buyer that the Goods can be collected or arranges delivery at the Warranty Provider’s expense.

The costs of delivering the Goods to the service point and collecting them after warranty repair are borne by the Warranty Provider if the defect has been accepted as covered by warranty. If the claim proves unjustified, transport and diagnostic costs are borne by the Buyer.

The Warranty Provider may issue the Buyer a warranty card in paper or electronic form. The lack of a warranty card does not deprive the Buyer of warranty rights - proof of purchase is sufficient to exercise them.

sections.heading: Complaint due to non-conformity of Goods with the Contract

blocks.text: The Seller is liable for non-conformity of the Goods with the Contract under the rules set out in the Act of 30 May 2014 on consumer rights - in relations with Consumers - and under the Civil Code - in relations with B2B Buyers.
The Seller is liable for non-conformity of the Goods with the Contract existing at the time of delivery and revealed within two years from that moment.

items: request repair of the Goods;
request replacement of the Goods with defect-free Goods;
request a Price reduction - if repair or replacement is impossible, excessively costly or the Seller has refused to perform it;
withdrawal from the Contract and refund of the full Price - if the non-conformity is material and repair or replacement proved ineffective or the Seller refused to perform it.

blocks.text: It is presumed that non-conformity revealed within one year of release of the Goods already existed at the time of delivery, unless the Seller proves otherwise.
In relations with B2B Buyers, statutory warranty liability is excluded pursuant to Article 558 § 1 of the Civil Code.
A B2B Buyer may pursue rights only under the Warranty described in the Bergson Machines Warranty Terms document or under terms individually agreed with the Seller in writing.

sections.heading: Right to withdraw from the Contract — Consumers

blocks.text: A Consumer who concluded the Contract remotely or outside business premises has the right to withdraw from it without giving a reason within 14 days from taking possession of the Goods.

The right of withdrawal does not apply where the Goods were manufactured or modified according to the Consumer’s individual specification, are Goods imported on special production order, or have clearly deteriorated for reasons attributable to the Consumer.

items: sending a clear withdrawal statement to e-mail: kontakt@bergsonmachines.pl or in writing to the Seller’s registered office address - before the 14-day deadline expires;
returning the Goods within 14 days from submitting the statement, in unchanged condition, if possible in the original packaging, to the address indicated by the Seller;
bearing the direct costs of returning the Goods, unless the Seller expressly agreed to cover them.

blocks.text: The Seller refunds all payments received, including standard delivery costs, without delay and no later than within 14 days from receiving the withdrawal statement. The Seller may withhold the refund until receiving the Goods or confirmation of their dispatch.

A complaint due to non-conformity of the Goods with the Contract or warranty rights should be submitted by e-mail, in writing or through the authorised Bergson Machines dealer from whom the Goods were purchased.

items: the Buyer’s first name, surname and contact details;
order number or VAT invoice number;
Goods serial number;
a precise description of the defect or non-conformity together with photo or video documentation;
the Buyer’s request, in particular repair, replacement, price reduction or refund.

blocks.text: The Seller reviews the complaint and replies within 14 calendar days in the case of a Consumer and 14 business days in the case of a B2B Buyer submitting a warranty complaint.
No response to a Consumer within 14 calendar days means the complaint is deemed justified. The response is sent by e-mail or in writing - at the Buyer’s request.

items: mediation conducted by the competent Trade Inspection Inspectorate;
proceedings before the Permanent Consumer Arbitration Court at the Trade Inspection;
online dispute resolution ODR platform: https://ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr.

blocks.text: The Seller is not obliged to use out-of-court dispute resolution methods, but may consent to participate in a specific procedure.

blocks.title: 1.2 t or 1.6 t - which mini excavator to choose?
blocks.text: The 1.2 t models work better for home and garden jobs and wherever passing through narrower spaces matters. The 1.6 t platform provides greater stability, working reach and more comfortable operation for regular earthworks and installation jobs.

blocks.title: How much does a mini excavator cost and what determines the price?
blocks.text: The price is mainly affected by the machine weight, engine, cab and selected attachments. The difference between the standard version and the Kubota engine variant mainly results from the power unit and the customer’s target work profile.

blocks.title: Mini excavator for the garden, installations and everyday earthworks
blocks.text: When choosing, not only the purchase price matters, but also service, parts and post-sale response speed. In practice, these elements determine whether the machine actually works and earns or waits for support.

blocks.title: 25, 30 or 40 kW generator - how to choose power?
blocks.text: Generator selection starts with the real power demand and whether the unit is to serve as backup or operate regularly. In smaller facilities, 25 kW is often enough, while company facilities, farms or construction sites more often require 30-40 kW.

blocks.title: What to consider besides generator power?
blocks.text: Not only the engine and rated power matter, but also the alternator type, ATS, AVR, control panel and access to service and parts. These elements decide whether the generator will be convenient in daily use and quickly return to work after service.

blocks.title: Generator for business, farm and field work
blocks.text: Silent generators work well as backup power for a company, farm, construction site and field work. A well-selected model should provide stable voltage, simple operation and a configuration matched to the actual load.
